_comment: UAE -> Norway booking. THE FIRST ROUTE BUILT FOR THE LIVE-SLOT FLOW. Norway has open slots, so there is no invitation, no 12-hour window and no email dependency — which makes it the cheapest place to learn the pages that every route shares: pick a slot, pay, confirm. Nobody has seen those on ANY route yet.
_comment_enabled: OFF, and it stays off until the whole flow has been walked in a browser. The selectors below are SCAFFOLDING — inherited guesses plus what the slot checker already proves — not captured DOM. A route is armed only when its committing step is known to be in the right place, and for Norway that means seeing the payment page.
_comment_why_new_flow: The live-slot flow, not the waitlist one. Nothing exists to resume: 'Start New Booking' CREATES the application, so there is no dashboard row to find and no identity to assert. That removes the riskiest part of booking (picking the wrong client's row) and leaves the part nobody has mapped (what happens after a slot is chosen).

steps.name: start_booking
steps._comment: PROVEN SELECTOR, borrowed rather than guessed: src/vfs_bot/slot_check.py:265 clicks exactly this on every hourly run across every route, so it is the one element here that is already known to work. It lands on Appointment Details.
steps._comment_entry: Marked explicitly even though the type implies it. This is the step the whole flow hangs off, and being able to read the mode without knowing the inference rules is worth the line.
steps._comment_before: POSITION MATTERS. A new step with no before/after is APPENDED, which put this after the committing slot pick — the flow would have picked a slot for an application it had not created yet. Steps run in order, so the entry step must be anchored to the front of the flow explicitly.

steps.name: appointment_details

fields.name: centre
fields.label: Choose your Application Centre
fields._comment: Addressed by "control" (the Angular formcontrolname), NOT by "selector". That choice routes the fill through slot_check.select_mat_dropdown, which the hourly slot checker uses on THESE SAME dropdowns on every run: it waits for the panel to populate (options arrive async, often behind a spinner and only after the parent dropdown API call), escalates a click an overlay intercepts, and logs the options that WERE offered when a value does not match. A raw "selector" takes the weaker generic path instead, which opened the overlay and found no options - all three dropdowns were left empty on the 2026-09-26 run.

steps._comment_url: OBSERVED: /are/en/nor/application-detail. It was previously "appointment", which NEVER matches that URL - so the step timed out waiting for a page it was already on, and never reached the dropdowns at all. steps.name: your_details
steps._comment: STEP 2 of 5. REAL DOM, supplied 2026-09-26. Angular's app-dynamic-form renders EVERY possible control as an <app-dynamic-control> wrapper and leaves the unused ones as empty comment placeholders, so the inputs cannot be addressed positionally. They are found by their visible LABEL, which is what the waitlist field engine already does.

fields.name: first_name
fields.label: First Name
fields._comment: maxlength=60. The input carries appuppercase, so VFS uppercases it regardless; doing it here keeps what we send identical to what the page displays.

fields.name: phone_country_code
fields.label: Contact number
fields._comment: TWO inputs share ONE 'Contact number' label — maxlength=3 then maxlength=15 — so they are addressed by index under that label. The same shape Switzerland already has.

fields.name: email
fields.label: Email
fields._comment: type=email, maxlength=50. This is the address VFS sends the invitation to, which is why it has to match the account mailbox the watcher reads.

steps._comment_dwell: *** THE PAGE ENFORCES A WAIT. *** It renders 'Warning: Please wait 4 seconds before saving your details and continuing'. Saving early is rejected. Switzerland's equivalent page demands 32s, so this number is PER ROUTE and must be read off the page rather than assumed. 10s gives margin over the stated 4 without inventing a longer delay.
steps._comment_submit: 'Save', NOT 'Continue'. This page offers Cancel / Save / Update, and the Update button is hidden. Clicking Continue here matches nothing.
steps._comment_url: NO url_contains: this page URL has never been observed, and a GUESSED gate is worse than none. A wrong gate blocks the step before it starts, which is exactly how appointment_details failed - it waited for "appointment" while sitting on /application-detail. Without a gate the step proceeds and fails on a real selector instead, which is diagnosable. Add the gate once the URL is seen.

appointment_type.label: Choose a slot

calendar._comment_available_day: *** date-availiable HAS THREE i's. *** VFS's own typo, in Norway's markup exactly as in Switzerland's. Matching the correct spelling finds nothing, and the run then reports no slots while the page is showing one.

Captured 2026-09-26: the calendar opened on OCTOBER with exactly one available day, data-date=2026-10-28, carrying
availiable

The base marks the slot pick as the commit point because for most of this project nobody had seen what came after it. Norway shows that selecting a slot reserves nothing - the commit is Pay Online on review_pay, six pages later. Left as an explicit false rather than deleted so the override is visible in the file instead of being an absence someone has to notice.
steps._comment_strategy: LATEST for now, which is a TESTING choice rather than a product one. The far end of the calendar is the least contended, so a trial run is least likely to take a slot a real applicant wanted today. Switch to "earliest" before this is used for a client: a waitlist slot is not held while the remaining pages are walked, so speed is what wins one.

steps._comment: 'Review' — the last page before money moves.

fields.name: accept_terms
fields.label: I accept the
fields._comment: Terms and Conditions. MANDATORY: 'Pay Online' is disabled="true" until this is ticked.
fields._comment_wrapper: *** THE REVIEW CHECKBOXES ARE NOT IN AN app-dynamic-control. *** Every other form page on this portal wraps its controls in that element, and the label-scoping locator defaults to it - so on this page it would match nothing and the step would fail exactly as appointment_details did. These two sit in <div class="ot-checkbox"> instead, because they are OneTrust consent controls rather than VFS dynamic-form controls. Caught by reading the DOM, not by running it.
fields._comment_index: No index: each checkbox has its OWN div.ot-checkbox wrapper, so the label alone identifies it. An index here would look inside a single wrapper that holds only one control.

fields.name: marketing_consent
fields.label: Yes, I agree to receive future communication
fields._comment: *** OPTIONAL, AND DELIBERATELY LEFT UNTICKED. *** This is marketing consent given on a real person's behalf. It is not required to book, so ticking it would consent them to something they never asked for. A human ticking it by hand is the operator's choice; it is not the bot's to make.

steps._comment_submit: 'Pay Online', addressed by id rather than label: it is an OneTrust consent-gated submit (class ot-submit-button) whose label text sits between comment nodes. disabled="true" until the terms box is ticked.
steps._comment_commits: *** THE REAL POINT OF NO RETURN, AND IT IS HERE. *** Clicking this leaves VFS entirely for https://secureacceptance.cybersource.com/checkout, a third-party payment gateway. Everything before it is reversible; this is not. The flag has MOVED OFF select_slot, where it sat as an admitted placeholder on every route because nobody had seen this page. That move is the main outcome of walking Norway.

steps.name: confirmation
steps._comment: Still removed. What follows 'Pay Online' is the CyberSource gateway, not a VFS confirmation page, so there is no VFS page here to describe yet.

_comment_flow_expected: Start New Booking -> Appointment Details (centre/category/sub) -> slot calendar -> ??? -> payment -> confirmed. Everything from the calendar onward is unknown on every route, which is the gap this walk exists to close.
_comment_next: Walk it with:  python -m src.booking probe -sc AE -dc NOR --walk --keep-open --hold 1800  — one login, capturing every page. Then write the real selectors, move commits to payment, and only then set enabled.
_comment_flow_real: CONFIRMED END TO END, 2026-09-26. VFS's own progress bar reads: 1 Appointment Details -> 2 Your Details -> 3 Book Appointment -> 4 Services -> 5 Review. The DOM adds a 'Your Details Summary' page between 2 and 3 that the bar does not number, so there are SIX VFS pages plus the external gateway. Fee captured: AED 84.67, the VFS service charge with no add-ons.
_comment_payment_gateway: AFTER 'Pay Online' the browser leaves VFS for https://secureacceptance.cybersource.com/checkout, which asks for billing name, address, city, country, postcode, phone and email, then CARD TYPE, NUMBER, EXPIRY and CVN. It RSA-encrypts the card fields in the browser before submitting (see the jwk input and RsaOaep.prepareFormForSubmission). NO CARD DETAILS EXIST ANYWHERE IN THIS SYSTEM AND NONE SHOULD: automating that page means holding a client's card, which is a different class of problem from booking and needs its own decision. The run stops at Pay Online.
